clue.text: Dickens's bush raptor as ill-fated gambler

parts.note: the mulberry is the bush of the nursery rhyme 'Here we go round the mulberry bush'
a hawk is a bird of prey, or raptor

explanation.surface: A predatory bird lurking in a Dickensian shrub turns out to be a doomed card-player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dickens's' places the character: Sir Mulberry Hawk is the dissolute gambler of Nicholas Nickleby, killed in a duel.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Mulberry Hawk, a rakish card-sharp in Nicholas Nickleby, dies in a duel, so his fate is unlucky.

clue.text: Greek girls possibly named as bacchantes

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of the words named as could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Some Greek girls might be given the title of followers of Bacchus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the seven letters of NAMED AS; 'Greek girls' merely sets the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Maenads were the frenzied female worshippers of Dionysus, also called bacchantes after his Roman name Bacchus.

clue.text: His widow was not sorry

parts.note: the widow is the title character of an operetta, and one who is not sorry is merry: the composer of The Merry Widow

explanation.surface: A dead man's wife did not mourn him.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehár composed the operetta The Merry Widow, so the merry widow is figuratively his.

clue.text: Eliot's weird, secret oak in Somerset

indicators.note: weird suggests the letters of secret oak are arranged strangely

explanation.surface: T. S. Eliot writes of a strange, mysterious oak tree in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weird' rearranges SECRET OAK; 'in Somerset' locates the village that gives its name to Eliot's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The second of T. S. Eliot's Four Quartets is named after the Somerset village where his ancestors lived.

clue.text: Where John Gilpin lost his wig

definitions.text: Where John Gilpin lost his wig

parts.words: Where John Gilpin lost his wig
parts.note: in Cowper's comic ballad the runaway horse carries Gilpin off, and his hat and wig fly off along the highway

explanation.surface: A question about the comic misfortune of Cowper's runaway rider.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowper's ballad has Gilpin's hat and wig blown off as his horse bolts along the highway to Edmonton.

clue.text: Sussex town officer in Watsonian role

definitions.meaning: a seaside town in East Sussex, England, near the 1066 battle site
Captain Arthur ... is Poirot's companion and narrator, playing the part Dr Watson plays for Holmes

explanation.surface: A coastal resort is also a soldier cast as the detective's sidekick.
explanation.definitionFit: Hastings is both the East Sussex resort and Agatha Christie's army captain who chronicles Poirot's cases.

clue.text: Opera composer must add new ending for a disciple of Schoenberg

indicators.note: the answer must add a letter at its end to reach the disciple's name, so that letter is taken off the disciple

parts.note: Anton Webern studied with Arnold Schoenberg in Vienna

explanation.surface: An opera writer needs a fresh ending to become a pupil of the twelve-tone master.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: the answer plus N, at its 'ending', gives WEBERN, so N is removed from WEBERN.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Maria von Weber wrote the German romantic operas Der Freischütz and Oberon.

clue.text: Power to be added for foreign policy analyst and Pulitzer prizewinner

definitions.text: Power to be added for foreign policy analyst and Pulitzer prizewinner

parts.words: Power to be added for foreign policy analyst and Pulitzer prizewinner
parts.note: the given name of the writer and diplomat whose surname is Power, which must be added to complete her name

explanation.surface: A call to give more strength to a foreign-affairs expert and prize-winning author.
explanation.definitionFit: Samantha Power, later US ambassador to the UN, won a Pulitzer for her book on genocide, 'A Problem from Hell'.

clue.text: Souvenir of Rome I'm rewriting

indicators.note: rewriting means the letters of Rome I'm are set down in a new order

explanation.surface: A keepsake from the Italian capital that the writer is revising.
explanation.definitionFit: A written record of remembered events is a keepsake of the past, as the French souvenir means a memory.

clue.text: Mistaken identity for two Syracusans, funnily enough

definitions.text: Mistaken identity for two Syracusans, funnily enough

parts.words: Mistaken identity for two Syracusans, funnily enough
parts.note: in Shakespeare's farce The Comedy of Errors twin visitors from Syracuse are mistaken for their twin brothers, citizens of another city

explanation.surface: Two men from Syracuse are comically confused with others.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Comedy of Errors the Syracusan Antipholus and Dromio are taken for their twins, the citizens of Ephesus.

clue.text: He found endangered species fearfully balanced

definitions.text: He found endangered species fearfully balanced

parts.words: He found endangered species fearfully balanced
parts.note: the poet who asked what hand could frame the tiger's fearful symmetry; the tiger is now an endangered species

explanation.surface: A naturalist observing a threatened animal's alarming symmetry.
explanation.definitionFit: William Blake's 'The Tyger' asks what immortal hand could frame its 'fearful symmetry'.

clue.text: Whence Dinesen wrote

parts.note: Karen Dinesen's memoir is titled 'Out of' a continent, so that continent is the place she wrote from

explanation.surface: A question about the place from which the Danish author sent her writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Karen Blixen, born Dinesen, wrote 'Out of Africa' about her Kenyan coffee farm.

clue.text: Fa presto to embellish the Escorial

definitions.text: Fa presto to embellish the Escorial

parts.words: Fa presto to embellish the Escorial
parts.note: the Neapolitan painter nicknamed 'Luca fa presto' for his speed was called to Spain to paint frescoes in the Escorial palace

explanation.surface: An urging to decorate the Spanish royal palace quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Luca Giordano, known as 'Luca fa presto', painted ceiling frescoes at the Escorial for Charles II of Spain.

clue.text: Kipling established a company for him

definitions.text: Kipling established a company for him

parts.words: Kipling established a company for him
parts.note: Kipling's school stories are titled after their ringleader '& Co.', so the author gave him a company

explanation.surface: A businessman's tale of the writer founding a firm for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's book 'Stalky & Co.' follows the schoolboy Stalky and his two friends.

clue.text: "He still was strong and fresh, his brain was grey. / Such — might our young ladies move" (William Cartwright)

definitions.text: "He still was strong and fresh, his brain was grey. / Such — might our young ladies move" (William Cartwright)

parts.words: "He still was strong and fresh, his brain was grey. / Such — might our young ladies move" (William Cartwright)
parts.note: the missing word in Cartwright's lines names the quality of an old man still vigorous, whose grey hair shows his years

explanation.surface: A gap-fill quotation from the seventeenth-century poet William Cartwright about a vigorous old man.
explanation.definitionFit: Agedness is the state of being old, which a grey-haired but still strong man displays.

clue.text: "On the fore-stage, an — is addressing a tattered crowd"

definitions.text: "On the fore-stage, an — is addressing a tattered crowd"

parts.words: "On the fore-stage, an — is addressing a tattered crowd"
parts.note: the missing word names someone who stirs up a ragged crowd with speeches, a rabble-rouser

explanation.surface: A gap-fill stage direction showing a speaker haranguing a ragged mob.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone haranguing a crowd to stir it to protest is a rabble-rouser.

clue.text: Sadly no raga art available in cultural Spanish city

indicators.note: sadly suggests the letters of no raga art have gone wrong and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Unfortunately no Indian music or painting is to be found in a city full of culture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' rearranges NO RAGA ART; 'available in' just joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarragona is a Catalan port city rich in Roman remains, a World Heritage site.

clue.text: Put on finish with hesitation — seems there's more to come

parts.note: to put on is to add
a finish is an end
um is the sound of hesitating in speech

explanation.surface: Someone completes a task haltingly, sensing it is not quite over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seems' links the wordplay to the definition, which describes something tacked on afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An addendum is material appended to a book or document, extra matter supplementing it.

clue.text: Lawrence poem (part of the Great Hebridean cycle)

indicators.note: part of says the letters lie within the words the Great Hebridean, running across them

explanation.surface: A poem by D. H. Lawrence belongs to a cycle about the Scottish islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts with the last letter of 'Great' and ends inside 'Hebridean'; 'cycle' only dresses the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: D. H. Lawrence wrote a poem of that title about his dead mother lying like a young bride.

clue.text: Feline Capulet

parts.note: Juliet's fiery cousin is mocked by Mercutio as the 'Prince of Cats', after the cat in the Reynard fables

explanation.surface: A cat-like member of Juliet's family.
explanation.definitionFit: Tybalt, Juliet's cousin, shares his name with the cat Tibert in the Reynard tales, so Mercutio calls him 'Prince of Cats'.

clue.text: Rewrite a drama for the fleet

indicators.note: rewrite asks for the letters of a drama to be written out again in a different order

explanation.surface: An instruction to adapt a play for the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a great war fleet, as in the Spanish one sent against England in 1588.

clue.text: Composer uneasily nears Kentucky

indicators.note: uneasily suggests the letters of nears are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: KY is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Kentucky

explanation.surface: A musician approaches the Bluegrass State nervously.
explanation.definitionFit: Anton Arensky was a Russian Romantic composer, a pupil of Rimsky-Korsakov and teacher of Rachmaninov.

clue.text: Magistrates on mysterious path to humorous writer

parts.note: magistrates sitting in court are collectively the bench
a ley line is a supposed ancient track with mystical significance

explanation.surface: Justices follow a strange route to a comic author.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Benchley was an American humorist of the New Yorker and the Algonquin Round Table.

clue.text: New England stopover by John Irving

definitions.text: New England stopover by John Irving

parts.words: New England stopover by John Irving
parts.note: Irving's novel takes its name from a lodging place in New Hampshire, a New England state

explanation.surface: A traveller's overnight stay in New England near a novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: John Irving's novel 'The Hotel New Hampshire' is named after the family's inn in that New England state.

clue.text: Favourite shrub of Apollo

parts.note: the nymph Apollo loved was turned into a laurel, and her name is also that of a flowering evergreen bush

explanation.surface: The sun god's preferred garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The nymph Daphne, loved by Apollo, became a laurel; daphne is also a fragrant flowering shrub.

clue.text: Orphan from The Idiot

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the title The Idiot, running across both words

explanation.surface: An orphaned character taken from Dostoevsky's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Johanna Spyri's Heidi is an orphan sent to live with her grandfather in the Alps.

clue.text: Some distance away, we hear, like Carton's better thing?

definitions.meaning: Sydney Carton's last words call his deed 'a far, far better thing', so it is described as 'a far' better

explanation.surface: We are told something is remote, like the noble deed in A Tale of Two Cities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' flags that the second sense works as two spoken words, 'a far', rather than the written single word.
explanation.definitionFit: Being remote means lying at a distance; Carton's sacrifice is 'a far, far better thing'.

clue.text: Reported table of Hungarian composer

indicators.note: reported means the word is spoken out loud, giving a matching sound

parts.note: a table of items is a list

explanation.surface: A news report about the furniture of a Romantic pianist.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian virtuoso pianist and composer of the Hungarian Rhapsodies.

clue.text: Dancers spotted during the Lost Leader's wanderings

definitions.text: Dancers spotted during the Lost Leader's wanderings

parts.words: Dancers spotted during the Lost Leader's wanderings
parts.note: Browning's 'The Lost Leader' is taken to be Wordsworth, who wandered lonely as a cloud and saw golden flowers dancing

explanation.surface: A displaced chief roams about and sees some performers.
explanation.definitionFit: Wordsworth's 'I Wandered Lonely as a Cloud' describes a host of golden flowers 'dancing in the breeze'.

clue.text: Scott's early death

parts.note: early, as in the early days, means old, of former times
mortality is death or the fact of having to die

explanation.surface: Sir Walter Scott dies young.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Mortality is a Walter Scott novel of the Covenanters, named after an old man who restores their gravestones.
